---
title: "Methods in Microbiomics"
subtitle: "Hands-on lessons for analysing microbiome sequencing data"
toc: false
---

Lessons and best practices for robust, reproducible analysis of microbiome sequencing data, written by people who use these methods daily in the [Sunagawa group](https://micro.biol.ethz.ch/research/sunagawa.html) and the NCCR Microbiomes.

Every lesson is something you **do**, not just read:

- **Command-line steps** run in a ready-made cloud computer (GitHub Codespaces). The tools and data are already installed, so there's nothing to set up on your laptop.
- **Analysis steps** run in R **directly in this page**. Edit the code, run it, and check yourself with exercises.
- Each lesson ends with what changes when you go from the teaching data to a real project.

## Learning paths

::: {.path-card}
### I have shotgun metagenomes
**Gene catalogs: build, quantify, analyse.** Find the genes in your samples, measure how abundant they are per cell, and relate them to the environment.

[Start the lesson →](lessons/gene-catalogs/index.qmd)
:::
